_: Event cards (events.js; screen map D1; references: CK3's event pool, King of Dragon Pass's scenes). settings: on (the default for a reign that doesn't say, options.events), chance of a card each season (and in a breather, when only breatherDecks may be drawn), rest (seasons before a card may come again), noRepeatDecks (the last decks drawn, avoided while another is eligible), boost (weight for a deck while the realm builds to a crisis). cards: id, deck, subject (realm, crown_town, seat, hungry_town, house_cold, house_warm, house_any, war_pair), when (season, treasuryBelow/Above in gold, peaceBelow/Above, after/before as a share of the reign's clock, threat), weight, title and text ({town} {house} {lord} {rival} {season} filled from the realm), choices (label, cost in gold, favour {house|rival|all: n}, gold, ease (a director threat), text: what it did, later {in: seasons, text, favour, gold}), ignore (what doing nothing costs). Gold: 1 = 100 crowns. deadline: seasons the King has to answer a card from its rider's arrival (a card's own deadline overrides), then it lapses and doing nothing costs. rider.speed: tiles a season the rider rides from the card's town to the King's seat (the card is seen coming, riding, and not answered until he arrives).

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Rats in {town}'s granary
cards.text: The reeve of {town} brings a sack gnawed through. Half the winter's grain is fouled, and the town knows it.

choices.label: Buy grain from the coast
choices.text: Grain carts reach {town} before the rumour does.

choices.label: Ration it, and say so
choices.text: {town} tightens its belt, and grumbles.

later.text: {town} came through the lean months on short bread; they remember the King's honesty.

choices.label: Hang the granary keeper
choices.text: The keeper hangs in {town}'s square. The rats do not care.

ignore.text: {town} goes hungry, and blames the crown.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: The bridge at {town} is down
cards.text: Spring floods took the bridge at {town}. Carts go the long way round, and the market thins.

choices.label: Rebuild it in stone
choices.text: Masons come to {town}.

later.text: A stone bridge stands at {town}; trade comes back across it.

choices.label: A ferry, for now
choices.text: A ferry plies at {town}; it will do.

choices.label: Let the town see to it
choices.text: {town} is told to mend its own bridge.

ignore.text: {town}'s market dwindles without its bridge.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: Monks at the gates of {town}
cards.text: Grey-robed brothers ask leave to found a house near {town}. They will pray for the King, they say, and want land for it.

choices.label: Grant them land
choices.text: The brothers build. The great houses approve of a pious King.

later.text: The monks' fields near {town} feed the poor in a hard season.

choices.label: Let them preach, but no land
choices.text: The brothers preach in {town}'s square, and move on in spring.

choices.label: Turn them away
choices.text: The brothers leave cursing the King's name.

ignore.text: The brothers settle where they please, and say the crown would not hear them.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} asks a feast in {house}'s honour
cards.text: {lord} of {house} has served the crown well, and says so, loudly. A feast in their honour is expected.

choices.label: Feast them at Kingsmere
choices.text: {house} drinks the King's health until dawn.

choices.label: A gift in their hall instead
choices.text: {house} takes the gift, and notes it was not a feast.

choices.label: Remind them who serves whom
choices.text: {lord} goes home without a feast, and with a grudge.

later.text: {house} pays its levy late this year.

ignore.text: {house} waits for a feast that never comes.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {lord} mocks the King at table
cards.text: At {house}'s own table {lord} called the crown a beggar's hat. The words reached Kingsmere before the cups were cleared.

choices.label: Demand an apology
choices.text: {lord} apologises, through clenched teeth.

later.text: {house} keeps its tongue in check at court.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.text: The King laughs. Some lords think him weak for it.

choices.label: Fine {house} for it
choices.text: {house} pays the fine, and hates the paying.

ignore.text: The jest spreads; other lords repeat it.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: {house} and {rival} burn each other's villages
cards.text: The war between {house} and {rival} has spilled into farms. Refugees walk the King's roads.

choices.label: Take in the refugees
choices.text: The crown's towns open their gates to the burned-out.

choices.label: Back {house}
choices.text: The crown names {rival} the aggressor.

choices.label: Command them both to stop
choices.text: Heralds ride to both camps with the King's word.

later.text: The burning stops along the border, for now.

ignore.text: The burning spreads; the King's roads fill with the homeless.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Sellswords offer their swords
cards.text: A company of foreign spears camps outside Kingsmere. Their captain will fight for whoever pays first.

choices.label: Hire them for a season
choices.text: The sellswords take the King's silver and his orders.

choices.label: Pay them to leave
choices.text: The company marches on, a little richer.

choices.label: Drive them off
choices.text: The King's men chase the sellswords from the road.

later.text: The sellswords turn up in another lord's pay.

ignore.text: The sellswords find another master in the realm.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: A merchant hoards grain in {town}
cards.text: {town} starves while one merchant's cellar is full. The crowd knows whose.

choices.label: Seize the grain
choices.text: The King's men open the cellar to {town}.

choices.label: Buy it at his price
choices.text: The merchant grows rich; {town} eats.

choices.label: Let the market settle it
choices.text: {town} goes hungry while the price climbs.

later.text: A mob burns the merchant's house in {town}.

ignore.text: {town} riots against the hoarder, and against the crown that let him.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: The priests of {town} beg for bread
cards.text: The temple at {town} feeds the hungry from its own stores, and the stores are nearly gone.

choices.label: Fill the temple's stores
choices.text: Carts of grain reach the temple at {town}.

choices.label: Send a royal almoner
choices.text: The almoner keeps the temple's bread going a while longer.

choices.label: The temple can fend for itself
choices.text: The priests of {town} say the King is deaf.

ignore.text: The temple at {town} closes its doors; the hungry die at them.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A poet asks to sing the King's deeds
cards.text: A travelling poet wants a place at court. Pay him, and the taverns will sing what he writes.

choices.label: Keep him at court
choices.text: The poet's verses praise the King's wisdom.

later.text: The poet's song about the King is sung in every tavern.

choices.label: One night's purse
choices.text: The poet sings one night and leaves.

choices.label: Send him off
choices.text: The poet goes, and sings elsewhere, less kindly.

ignore.text: The poet writes a mocking verse instead.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: The tax men are cheating {town}
cards.text: {town} says the crown's collectors take twice what they hand in. The ledgers agree.

choices.label: Hang the collectors
choices.text: The collectors hang; the coin they stole returns to the treasury.

choices.label: Quietly replace them
choices.text: New collectors ride to {town}.

choices.label: Let it pass: the crown needs coin
choices.text: The collectors keep collecting.

ignore.text: {town} stops paying anyone at all.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A rich harvest
cards.text: The barns are full across the realm. The lords would have a share of the King's good fortune.

choices.label: Lower the tithe this year
choices.text: The realm rejoices at a lighter tithe.

choices.label: Store it against hard years
choices.text: Royal granaries fill.

later.text: In a lean season the royal granaries feed the realm.

choices.label: Sell the surplus abroad
choices.text: Foreign silver flows into the treasury.

ignore.text: The surplus rots; the lords ask what the King was thinking.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Snow cuts {town} off
cards.text: Drifts close the roads to {town}. Firewood and bread will not last the month.

choices.label: Send soldiers to clear the roads
choices.text: The King's men dig {town} out.

choices.label: Open the royal woods for firewood
choices.text: {town} burns the King's trees, and lives.

choices.label: Wait for the thaw
choices.text: {town} waits.

later.text: The thaw finds {town} thinner, and bitter.

ignore.text: {town} freezes through the dark weeks.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {lord} asks a royal tutor for an heir
cards.text: {house}'s heir is of an age to learn. {lord} asks that the King's own tutor teach the child.

choices.label: Lend the tutor
choices.text: The tutor goes to {house}.

later.text: {house}'s heir grows up loyal to the crown that taught them.

choices.label: Invite the heir to Kingsmere instead
choices.text: {house}'s heir comes to court, under the King's eye.

choices.label: The tutor is the King's
choices.text: {lord} hears no.

ignore.text: {house} takes the silence as a slight.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: A spy of {house} is caught
cards.text: A servant at Kingsmere was copying the King's letters for {house}. {lord} denies everything.

choices.label: Hang the spy and send the head to {lord}
choices.text: The head arrives at {house}'s gate.

choices.label: Turn the spy
choices.text: The spy now writes what the King wants {house} to read.

later.text: False letters lead {house} astray.

choices.label: Quietly send the spy home
choices.text: {lord} takes the mercy for weakness, or for courtesy.

ignore.text: The spy keeps copying the King's letters.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Sickness in {town}
cards.text: A fever has come to {town}. The healers want the gates shut; the merchants want them open.

choices.label: Shut the gates
choices.text: {town}'s gates close; the fever stays inside.

later.text: The fever burns out in {town}; it went no further.

choices.label: Send physicians
choices.text: Royal physicians ride to {town}.

choices.label: Keep trade flowing
choices.text: {town}'s gates stay open.

later.text: The fever spreads along the trade roads from {town}.

ignore.text: The fever spreads from {town}.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The lords want a tourney
cards.text: Peace makes young knights restless. The great houses ask for a tourney at Kingsmere.

choices.label: Hold a grand tourney
choices.text: Banners of every house fly over the lists at Kingsmere.

choices.label: A modest joust
choices.text: A day of jousting pleases the young knights.

choices.label: No tourney this year
choices.text: The knights grumble, and drink.

ignore.text: The young knights find other ways to spend their spirit.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: An envoy under a white branch
cards.text: A rider comes from where the trouble grows. Terms, perhaps, or a trick.

choices.label: Hear the terms, and pay them
choices.text: The envoy leaves with silver; the trouble eases.

choices.label: Send the envoy back unheard
choices.text: The envoy rides back angry.

choices.label: Hold the envoy hostage
choices.text: The envoy waits in the King's cells.

later.text: Word of the hostage spreads; no envoy will trust the crown now.

ignore.text: The envoy goes home with nothing; the trouble grows.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: A relic is found at {town}
cards.text: Diggers at {town} found bones the priests call holy. Pilgrims are already coming.

choices.label: Build a shrine for it
choices.text: A shrine rises at {town}.

later.text: Pilgrims bring silver to {town}'s shrine.

choices.label: Bring it to Kingsmere
choices.text: The relic comes to the King's own chapel.

choices.label: Call it a fraud
choices.text: The priests are scandalised.

ignore.text: A lord takes the relic for his own chapel.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The wells run low
cards.text: No rain since spring. The fields crack and the lords look to Kingsmere.

choices.label: Dig new wells across the realm
choices.text: Royal wells are dug from coast to hills.

choices.label: Pray for rain
choices.text: The temples pray.

later.text: Rain comes at last; the priests take the credit.

choices.label: Each house to its own wells
choices.text: The lords dig, and curse the King.

ignore.text: The harvest withers; the realm will be hungry this winter.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Wolves at {town}'s folds
cards.text: Three winters' lambs are gone from the hills above {town}. The shepherds want the King's huntsmen.

choices.label: Send the royal huntsmen
choices.text: The huntsmen ride out with dogs and spears.

later.text: Wolf pelts hang over {town}'s gate; the shepherds drink to the King.

choices.label: A bounty on every pelt
choices.text: Every lad in {town} takes a bow to the hills.

choices.label: Let the shepherds guard their own
choices.text: The shepherds sit up nights, and say what they think of Kingsmere.

ignore.text: The wolves grow bold; {town} loses more than lambs.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: A dead dog in {town}'s well
cards.text: Someone threw a dead dog down {town}'s well. The street blames the tanners; the tanners blame the street.

choices.label: Dig a new well
choices.text: Diggers sink a fresh well by {town}'s market.

choices.label: Find who did it
choices.text: The reeve asks questions up and down {town}.

later.text: The culprit was a jilted miller; {town} laughs about it now.

choices.label: Boil the water and say no more
choices.text: {town} boils its water, and grumbles over the fires.

ignore.text: {town} drinks foul water; the fever-carts come out.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: {town} wants a market day
cards.text: The guildsmen of {town} ask a royal charter for a weekly market. The neighbouring towns already have one.

choices.label: Grant the charter
choices.text: The King's seal goes on {town}'s charter.

later.text: {town}'s market day draws carts from three valleys; the crown takes its toll.

choices.label: Grant it, for a fee
choices.text: {town} pays for its charter, and expects much of it.

choices.label: One market is enough for that road
choices.text: {town}'s guildsmen go home with nothing.

ignore.text: {town} holds a market anyway, and pays no toll on it.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: {town}'s great bell has cracked
cards.text: The bell that rang for every birth and burial in {town} split in the frost. The town feels it as an omen.

choices.label: Cast a new one at the crown's cost
choices.text: Bell-founders come to {town} with clay and bronze.

later.text: The new bell rings over {town}; they say it has the King's voice.

choices.label: Let the town pay for it
choices.text: {town} passes the plate for its bell.

choices.label: A bell is a bell
choices.text: The cracked bell rings flat over {town}.

ignore.text: {town} hears the flat bell every hour, and thinks of the crown.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: An apprentice runs off with the guild's silver
cards.text: A smith's boy of {town} fled with the guild chest. The guild wants him hunted down.

choices.label: Hunt him down
choices.text: Riders go out on every road from {town}.

later.text: The boy is caught at a ford; the silver comes back short.

choices.label: Repay the guild from the treasury
choices.text: The guild of {town} is made whole by the crown.

choices.label: The guild should keep better boys
choices.text: The guild of {town} does not forget it.

ignore.text: The guild of {town} raises its prices to cover the loss.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: The river took {town}'s mill
cards.text: The spring flood tore the wheel off {town}'s mill. No flour until it turns again.

choices.label: Rebuild it now
choices.text: Millwrights work through the nights at {town}.

choices.label: Rebuild it higher up the bank
choices.text: A new mill rises above the flood line.

later.text: The next flood passes {town}'s mill by; the miller blesses the King's foresight.

choices.label: Grind by hand till summer
choices.text: {town} grinds by hand, and its bread is coarse.

ignore.text: {town} buys flour from upriver at a robber's price.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Fire in {town}'s poor quarter
cards.text: A lamp tipped over and half a street of {town} burned. Families bed down in the square.

choices.label: Rebuild the street
choices.text: Timber carts roll into {town} under the crown's mark.

choices.label: Open the royal stores to them
choices.text: The burned-out of {town} eat the King's bread this season.

choices.label: They will build again; they always do
choices.text: {town}'s poor rebuild with what they can scavenge.

later.text: The rebuilt street in {town} is tinder again; folk say the next fire is the King's.

ignore.text: {town}'s homeless crowd the roads to Kingsmere.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: {town} accuses a widow of witchcraft
cards.text: A herb-woman of {town} is blamed for a dead calf and a stillborn child. The crowd has a rope.

choices.label: Spare her, and say why
choices.text: The King's word stops the rope; some in {town} mutter.

later.text: The widow's herbs save a child in {town}; the town's tongue turns.

choices.label: Let the priests try her
choices.text: The temple of {town} sits in judgement.

choices.label: Give the crowd what it wants
choices.text: The rope is used in {town}'s square.

ignore.text: {town} hangs her without the King's leave.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Bandits on the {town} road
cards.text: Merchants will not travel to {town} without a guard. The outlaws hide in the old forest.

choices.label: Clear the forest with soldiers
choices.text: The King's men beat the forest for a week.

later.text: The {town} road is safe again; carts come back.

choices.label: Pardon any who lay down their bows
choices.text: Some outlaws come in for the pardon; some laugh at it.

later.text: Pardoned outlaws keep the {town} road for the King now.

choices.label: Let the merchants hire guards
choices.text: The merchants hire guards, and add the cost to their prices.

ignore.text: Trade with {town} dries up; the outlaws grow fat.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: Beggars at the gates of {town}
cards.text: The roads have brought every hungry man in the realm to the King's own gate. The guards ask what to do.

choices.label: Feed them at the gate
choices.text: Soup kettles steam at {town}'s gate every morning.

choices.label: Put them to work on the walls
choices.text: The beggars haul stone for bread.

later.text: The beggars' wall stands; some stayed on as masons.

choices.label: Drive them from the gate
choices.text: The guards clear the gate with staves.

ignore.text: The beggars camp at the gate; the lords step over them.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The court fool mocks the Hand
cards.text: At supper the fool aped the Hand's walk so well that the hall roared. The Hand did not.

choices.label: Reward the fool
choices.text: The fool gets a silver bell. The Hand gets a sour look.

choices.label: Make the fool apologise
choices.text: The fool apologises in rhyme, which is worse.

later.text: The rhyme has reached every tavern in {town}.

choices.label: Whip the fool
choices.text: The hall goes quiet when the fool is led out.

ignore.text: The fool does it again the next night, to more laughter.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The priests want a greater temple
cards.text: The high priest says {town}'s temple is too small for a king's prayers. He has drawings.

choices.label: Build it, whatever it costs
choices.text: Masons from three realms come to {town}.

later.text: The great temple of {town} is hallowed; lords come from every house to see it.

choices.label: A new roof will do
choices.text: The old temple gets a new lead roof.

choices.label: The gods hear prayers in small rooms too
choices.text: The high priest rolls up his drawings, slowly.

ignore.text: The high priest preaches on kings who forget the gods.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: Clipped coin in the treasury
cards.text: The master of the mint shows the King a fistful of crowns, every one shaved at the rim.

choices.label: Recoin the whole treasury
choices.text: The mint runs day and night to strike honest coin.

later.text: Merchants trust the crown's coin again; the tolls come in full.

choices.label: Hang the clippers when found
choices.text: Gibbets go up by {town}'s mint.

choices.label: Shave the next coinage too
choices.text: The crown's coin goes out lighter, and the crown a little richer.

later.text: Foreign merchants weigh the King's coin and laugh.

ignore.text: Clipped coin passes through every market in the realm.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Pilgrims crowd the roads
cards.text: A holy year brings pilgrims to every shrine. Innkeepers grow rich; constables grow tired.

choices.label: Build hostels on the pilgrim roads
choices.text: Hostels with the crown's sign go up along the roads.

later.text: Pilgrims pray for the King in every hostel he built.

choices.label: Toll the pilgrims
choices.text: Every pilgrim pays a penny at the crown's bridges.

choices.label: Let them pass as they will
choices.text: The roads fill, and empty, as they always have.

ignore.text: A pilgrim crush at a ford drowns a dozen; the priests ask where the King was.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A comet over the realm
cards.text: A tailed star hangs in the night sky. The priests say it means a king's death; the astrologers, a king's triumph.

choices.label: Pay the astrologers to proclaim it
choices.text: Criers read the astrologers' happy reading in every town.

choices.label: Hold a great sacrifice
choices.text: Oxen burn at every temple in the King's name.

choices.label: It is a star, and nothing more
choices.text: Some lords think the King brave; more think him rash.

later.text: The comet fades and the King still lives; the doubters go quiet.

ignore.text: Every lord reads the comet his own way.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A foreign queen sends gifts
cards.text: Across the sea a queen sends silks and a white horse, and asks nothing yet.

choices.label: Send richer gifts back
choices.text: Gold and a falcon sail to the queen.

later.text: The foreign queen's ships trade freely in the King's ports.

choices.label: A courteous letter
choices.text: A letter goes back, warm and empty.

choices.label: Keep the horse and say nothing
choices.text: The queen hears nothing, and remembers it.

later.text: The foreign queen's ships tax the King's merchants.

ignore.text: The white horse grazes at Kingsmere; the queen waits for a word.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Salt is dear this year
cards.text: The salt pans flooded and the price has tripled. No salt, no salted meat for winter.

choices.label: Buy salt for the realm
choices.text: Salt carts carry the crown's barrels to every town.

choices.label: Fix the price by decree
choices.text: Salt is sold at the King's price, where it is sold at all.

later.text: Salt merchants hide their stock; the markets go short.

choices.label: Tax the salt merchants' windfall
choices.text: The crown takes its share of the dear salt.

ignore.text: Winter comes on unsalted meat; the realm eats poorly.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The steward wants a count of the realm
cards.text: Every hearth, every plough, every head of cattle. The steward says the crown is being cheated blind.

choices.label: Count it all
choices.text: The King's clerks ride out with ledgers.

later.text: The count is done; the tithe comes in fuller.

choices.label: Count the crown's own towns only
choices.text: Clerks count the royal towns, which grumble alone.

later.text: The royal towns' count turns up hidden fields.

choices.label: A count makes enemies
choices.text: The steward closes his ledger, unhappily.

ignore.text: The steward keeps guessing, and guessing low.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A ship of the dead in harbour
cards.text: A merchantman drifted in with its crew dead at the oars. The dockers will not touch it.

choices.label: Burn the ship where it lies
choices.text: The ship burns in the harbour mouth, its cargo with it.

later.text: Whatever killed that crew came no further.

choices.label: Salvage the cargo first
choices.text: The crown's men unload spices and silk, wrapped in cloth.

later.text: A fever runs along the docks.

choices.label: Tow it out to sea
choices.text: The ship drifts away on the tide, somewhere else's trouble.

ignore.text: Thieves strip the ship by night.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: A chain across the river below {town}
cards.text: Someone has strung a chain across the river and charges every barge. {town}'s trade chokes.

choices.label: Cut the chain
choices.text: Royal men cut the chain at dawn.

choices.label: Buy out the toll
choices.text: The crown pays the chain's owner to take it down.

choices.label: Put the crown's own toll there
choices.text: The chain stays; the King's men collect.

later.text: {town}'s merchants move their trade to the road.

ignore.text: {town}'s barges pay twice, and the town pays for it.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Gold in the hills by {town}
cards.text: A shepherd found yellow stones in a stream above {town}. Every chancer in the realm is on the road.

choices.label: Claim it for the crown
choices.text: Royal miners stake the hill above {town}.

later.text: The mine above {town} sends its first chest to Kingsmere.

choices.label: Let anyone dig and tax the finds
choices.text: {town} fills with diggers and quarrels.

choices.label: Reward the shepherd and seal it
choices.text: The shepherd gets a purse; the stream gets a guard.

ignore.text: Diggers tear up the hill and fight over it; the gold goes into their pockets.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Hail flattens the barley
cards.text: A summer storm laid the fields flat from the coast to the hills. The lords count their losses aloud.

choices.label: Forgive a season's tithe
choices.text: The houses keep their tithe this season.

choices.label: Lend seed for a second sowing
choices.text: Seed carts go out under the crown's mark.

later.text: A late harvest comes in thin but whole.

choices.label: Every house bears its own luck
choices.text: The lords bear it, and bear it in mind.

ignore.text: The realm tightens its belt for winter.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The spring fair at {town}
cards.text: Players, jugglers and a dancing bear want a pitch at {town}'s fair. The King's own presence would be a wonder.

choices.label: Open the fair yourself
choices.text: The King cuts the ribbon; the crowd cheers itself hoarse.

choices.label: Charge the players for their pitch
choices.text: The fair pays the crown its share.

choices.label: No bears in the King's city
choices.text: The bear goes back up the road, dancing.

ignore.text: The fair goes on, and nobody asks the King.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Midsummer fires at {town}
cards.text: The young of {town} want to leap the bonfires as their grandfathers did. The priests call it heathen.

choices.label: Light the fires, and join them
choices.text: The King's health is drunk around {town}'s fires.

choices.label: Side with the priests
choices.text: The fires stay dark; the young sulk.

choices.label: Let the town decide
choices.text: {town} decides, loudly, both ways.

ignore.text: The fires burn without the King's blessing; the priests write to Kingsmere.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: {town} asks the King to its harvest home
cards.text: The last sheaf is in. {town} would like the King at its table, or at least his wine.

choices.label: Send a cart of wine
choices.text: {town} drinks to the King until the barrels are dry.

choices.label: Go in person
choices.text: The King sits at {town}'s long table; they will talk of it for years.

later.text: {town} still tells of the night the King came to harvest home.

choices.label: The King has his own harvest to count
choices.text: {town} feasts without him.

ignore.text: {town} feasts, and notes the empty chair.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: The river freezes at {town}
cards.text: Ice a hand thick from bank to bank. The boats are stuck, but a road has opened where none was.

choices.label: Run carts across the ice
choices.text: Carts cross the river at {town} all winter.

later.text: A cart went through the ice at {town}; the town mourns.

choices.label: Mark a safe crossing
choices.text: The King's men stake a safe road across the ice.

choices.label: Forbid the ice
choices.text: The ice stays empty; the boats wait for spring.

ignore.text: Folk cross where they like, and some don't come back.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The white stag
cards.text: The huntsmen have found a white stag in the royal forest. The lords want to ride with the King.

choices.label: Ride out with all the lords
choices.text: Horns sound from the forest all day.

choices.label: Hunt it alone
choices.text: The King brings back the white stag himself.

later.text: The white stag's antlers hang in the hall; the lords who weren't asked look at them.

choices.label: Let the stag run
choices.text: The stag stays in the forest; the huntsmen sigh.

ignore.text: A lord's son kills the white stag, and boasts.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: Old soldiers at the gate
cards.text: Men who bled for the King's father beg at the gate on crutches. They ask what was promised.

choices.label: Pensions for every one
choices.text: The old soldiers draw their pay at Kingsmere.

later.text: Old soldiers drill the young levy for the King, unasked.

choices.label: A hall for them to live in
choices.text: An old barracks becomes a home for the King's veterans.

choices.label: That was the old King's promise
choices.text: The veterans go, cursing two kings now.

ignore.text: The old soldiers die at the gate one by one; the guards stop counting.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Good stone near {town}
cards.text: Masons say the hill by {town} is fine pale stone, the kind temples are built of.

choices.label: Open a royal quarry
choices.text: Quarrymen cut into the hill by {town}.

later.text: Pale stone from {town} sells across the realm.

choices.label: Let {town} quarry it
choices.text: {town} sells the stone and keeps the silver.

choices.label: Leave the hill be
choices.text: The hill keeps its stone.

ignore.text: A great house quarries it without asking.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The sun goes dark at noon
cards.text: For a quarter hour the sky went black. Cattle lay down; men knelt in the fields.

choices.label: Proclaim it a blessing on the King
choices.text: The temples call it the gods' wink at their chosen king.

choices.label: Fast and pray across the realm
choices.text: A day of fasting is called; the realm prays with the King.

choices.label: Let the priests sort it out
choices.text: The priests sort it out, each his own way.

ignore.text: Prophets in every market say the King's days are numbered.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A boy claims royal blood
cards.text: A beggar's boy in the north says he is the King's half-brother. He has a ring, and the old nurse backs him.

choices.label: Bring him to court and look at him
choices.text: The boy comes to Kingsmere, wide-eyed.

later.text: The boy grows up at court, the King's man; the rumour dies with the nurse.

choices.label: Pay the nurse to recant
choices.text: The nurse recants, richer.

choices.label: Have him taken quietly
choices.text: The boy is not seen again.

later.text: A lord says the boy was murdered by the crown.

ignore.text: A great house takes the boy in, and feeds the rumour.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: A monk of {town} copies books for coin
cards.text: A monk at {town} sells copied psalters to merchants. His abbot says it shames the order.

choices.label: Buy his books for the crown's library
choices.text: The King's library grows by a shelf.

later.text: Clerks taught from {town}'s books keep the King's accounts honest.

choices.label: Side with the abbot
choices.text: The monk goes back to his prayers.

choices.label: Let him sell, and tax it
choices.text: The monk pays the crown's tithe on his ink.

ignore.text: The monk keeps copying, and the abbot keeps writing to Kingsmere.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Smugglers in {town}'s cove
cards.text: Wine and silk come ashore at night by {town}, and none of it pays duty.

choices.label: Set a watch on the cove
choices.text: The King's men watch the cove all season.

later.text: The smugglers are caught with a full boat; the cargo is the crown's.

choices.label: Take a cut and look away
choices.text: The smugglers pay the crown to keep its lanterns dark.

choices.label: Hang the first one you catch
choices.text: A smuggler hangs at {town}'s quay.

ignore.text: {town}'s merchants buy from the cove and stop paying at the quay.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: {town}'s tithe barn burns
cards.text: The barn that held the crown's share of {town}'s harvest went up in a night. Some say it was no accident.

choices.label: Find who lit it
choices.text: The reeve's men question half of {town}.

later.text: It was the tithe-reeve himself, hiding his thefts.

choices.label: Rebuild and say nothing
choices.text: A new barn rises at {town}.

choices.label: Make {town} pay the tithe again
choices.text: {town} pays twice, and hates the crown for it.

ignore.text: {town} keeps its harvest this year, by fire.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} offers a daughter's hand
cards.text: {lord} of {house} would wed a daughter to the King's nephew. A bond of blood, and a claim with it.

choices.label: Accept the match
choices.text: Bells ring at {town} for the betrothal.

later.text: A child of both houses is born; {house} is the crown's kin now.

choices.label: Ask for a richer dowry
choices.text: {lord} haggles, and pays.

choices.label: Decline with honour
choices.text: {lord} takes the refusal politely, and coldly.

ignore.text: {lord} weds the daughter elsewhere.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {house}'s tribute is late again
cards.text: Two seasons now {house} has sent excuses instead of silver. {lord} pleads poor harvests at {town}.

choices.label: Send collectors with spears
choices.text: Royal spears ride into {town} to count {house}'s silver.

later.text: {house} pays on time now, and hates every coin of it.

choices.label: Forgive it this once
choices.text: {lord} thanks the King, and wonders how far it goes.

later.text: {house}'s tribute is late again.

choices.label: Take a hostage instead
choices.text: {house}'s heir comes to court as the King's guest.

later.text: The heir of {house} grows fond of Kingsmere.

ignore.text: Other houses note that {house} pays nothing, and wonder why they do.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: An heir is born to {house}
cards.text: {lord}'s wife has borne a son at {town}. The bells have rung there for a day and a night.

choices.label: Send a golden cup
choices.text: A gold cup with the crown's mark goes to {town}.

choices.label: Stand as the child's godfather
choices.text: The King's name is spoken over the font at {town}.

later.text: {house}'s heir, the King's godson, rides to court sworn to him.

choices.label: A letter of good wishes
choices.text: A letter goes to {town}.

ignore.text: {lord} counts the gifts and finds none from Kingsmere.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {lord} lies dying
cards.text: {lord} of {house} has taken to bed and will not rise. The question is who rules {town} after.

choices.label: Back the eldest son
choices.text: The King's word goes to the eldest; {house} is settled.

choices.label: Back the clever daughter
choices.text: The daughter rules {house} by the King's leave; the son sulks.

later.text: The daughter of {house} rules well, and remembers who backed her.

choices.label: Let {house} sort it out
choices.text: {house} argues over the deathbed.

ignore.text: {house} splits over the succession; brothers glare across {town}'s hall.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} wants a grander title
cards.text: {lord} of {house} has served well and would be called Duke. It costs the crown nothing but pride.

choices.label: Make {lord} a Duke
choices.text: Heralds proclaim the Duke of {town}.

choices.label: A title for the heir, later
choices.text: {lord} is promised; {lord} waits.

later.text: {lord} asks again about the promised title.

choices.label: Titles are earned on the field
choices.text: {lord} goes home to earn it.

ignore.text: {lord} styles themself Duke anyway, in letters.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {house} is drowning in debt
cards.text: {lord} owes moneylenders more than {town} earns in five years. They ask the crown to stand surety.

choices.label: Pay the debt outright
choices.text: {house}'s debt is the crown's now, and paid.

choices.label: Lend at fair interest
choices.text: The crown becomes {house}'s banker.

later.text: {house} repays the crown's loan with interest.

choices.label: {house} made its bed
choices.text: The moneylenders move into {town}.

ignore.text: The moneylenders seize {house}'s mills at {town}.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {lord} wants a better seat at table
cards.text: {lord} of {house} is tired of sitting below the salt. Someone must move down for {lord} to move up.

choices.label: Raise {lord} up
choices.text: {lord} sits nearer the King; another lord sits further off.

choices.label: Seat the lords by lot
choices.text: Every feast the seats are drawn by lot. Everyone is equally annoyed.

choices.label: The seats stay as they are
choices.text: {lord} sits below the salt and chews hard.

ignore.text: {lord} stops coming to feasts.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {house} builds a fort facing Kingsmere
cards.text: New walls rise on {house}'s side of the river, and their arrow slits look toward the crown's lands.

choices.label: Order it torn down
choices.text: The King's order is read at {town}'s gate.

later.text: {house} pulls the fort down stone by stone, slowly.

choices.label: Build one facing back
choices.text: The crown's masons answer stone with stone.

choices.label: Ask {lord} why, kindly
choices.text: {lord} says it faces the wolves, not the King.

later.text: The fort facing Kingsmere is manned now.

ignore.text: The fort is finished, and filled with spears.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} offers the crown a loan
cards.text: {house} has silver to spare and loyalty to show. {lord} would lend the crown a chest, at a kind rate.

choices.label: Take the loan
choices.text: {house}'s silver comes to Kingsmere.

later.text: {house} asks for its silver back, with interest.

choices.label: Ask a gift, not a loan
choices.text: {lord} gives, with a smile that slips.

choices.label: The crown needs no lender
choices.text: {lord} keeps the silver, and the offer stands.

ignore.text: {lord} lends it to a rival house instead.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {lord} refuses to come to court
cards.text: Summoned three times, {lord} of {house} sends only letters. They say {lord} fears the King's justice.

choices.label: Promise safe conduct
choices.text: {lord} comes to Kingsmere under the King's word.

later.text: {lord} kneels at court, and the realm sees the King's word kept.

choices.label: Declare {lord} outlaw
choices.text: {lord}'s name is read out at every market cross.

choices.label: Send a fourth summons
choices.text: The fourth letter goes to {town}.

ignore.text: {house} rules {town} as if there were no King.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {lord} sends a sick horse as a gift
cards.text: {house} sent the King a horse that coughed itself dead in the royal stable. The grooms say it was ill when it came.

choices.label: Take it as an insult
choices.text: {lord} hears the King's anger, and protests their innocence.

choices.label: Send a sick horse back
choices.text: A coughing nag arrives at {town}; {house} gets the joke, or doesn't.

later.text: {lord} laughs about the horse at court; the two of you are easier.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.text: The grooms bury the horse.

ignore.text: The grooms gossip; the court hears that {house} sent the King a dead horse.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {lord}'s bastard asks for a name
cards.text: A bastard of {house} has fought well under the King's banner and asks to bear the house's name.

choices.label: Legitimise them
choices.text: The King's seal makes a new heir of {house}.

later.text: The legitimised bastard of {house} is the King's most loyal sword.

choices.label: Knight them instead
choices.text: A new knight kneels before the King, nameless but honoured.

choices.label: A bastard is a bastard
choices.text: They go back to the ranks.

ignore.text: The bastard joins a rival's household.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: {house} asks the King to judge its war
cards.text: {lord} of {house} comes to Kingsmere with a list of {rival}'s crimes, and asks the King to name the guilty.

choices.label: Name {rival} guilty
choices.text: The crown's judgement goes against {rival}.

choices.label: Name both guilty
choices.text: Both houses are fined for breaking the King's peace.

choices.label: Hear {rival}'s side first
choices.text: Heralds ride to {rival} for its account.

later.text: Both houses have stated their case; the court is tired of it.

ignore.text: {house} decides the King has no judgement to give.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: {rival} holds {house}'s knights
cards.text: A dozen knights of {house} sit in {rival}'s cells. {lord} begs the King to buy them out.

choices.label: Pay the ransom
choices.text: The knights ride home to {town} on the crown's silver.

choices.label: Order {rival} to free them
choices.text: The King's order goes to {rival}.

later.text: {rival} frees half the knights, and keeps the rich ones.

choices.label: A war's prisoners are a war's business
choices.text: {lord} goes home empty-handed.

ignore.text: {house}'s knights rot in {rival}'s cells.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: {house} and {rival} fight over a ford
cards.text: One crossing on the river, two houses that want it. Every week a few more men drown in it.

choices.label: Give the ford to the crown
choices.text: The King's men hold the ford; both houses pay to cross.

later.text: The ford's tolls come to Kingsmere every season.

choices.label: Give it to {house}
choices.text: {house} holds the ford by the King's grant.

choices.label: Build a second bridge
choices.text: Masons build a bridge upriver; neither house need fight.

ignore.text: The ford runs red every spring.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: A peace feast for {house} and {rival}
cards.text: A herald says both houses are tired. A feast at the King's table might end it, or start it again over the wine.

choices.label: Host the feast
choices.text: {house} and {rival} drink at Kingsmere, swords at the door.

later.text: The peace made at the King's table holds through the season.

choices.label: Make them swear on the relics
choices.text: Both lords swear peace before the gods.

choices.label: Let them bleed
choices.text: The King has better uses for wine.

ignore.text: The war goes on; the herald goes home.

cards.subject: war_pair
cards.title: {house} sends the King a share of plunder
cards.text: {lord} has sacked one of {rival}'s villages and sends the crown a cart of silver plate.

choices.label: Take it
choices.text: The plate goes to the treasury; {rival} hears of it.

choices.label: Send it back to {rival}
choices.text: The plate goes home to {rival} with the King's regrets.

choices.label: Give it to the burned village
choices.text: The village gets its plate back, and a new roof.

later.text: The village tells everyone the King is just.

ignore.text: The plate sits in the courtyard; everyone knows whose it was.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} asks leave to go to war
cards.text: {house} has an old grudge against a neighbour, and {lord} wants the King's blessing to settle it.

choices.label: Give your blessing
choices.text: {lord} rides out with the King's leave.

later.text: {house} comes home with new fields, and new enemies.

choices.label: Forbid it
choices.text: {lord} sheathes the sword, for now.

choices.label: Settle the grudge at court
choices.text: The King hears both houses and splits the difference.

ignore.text: {lord} goes to war without asking.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: Bread riot in {town}
cards.text: The bakers of {town} have no flour and the crowd thinks they are lying. Ovens are being smashed.

choices.label: Send grain and soldiers
choices.text: Carts and spears roll into {town} together.

choices.label: Soldiers only
choices.text: The King's men clear {town}'s streets with staves.

later.text: {town} remembers the staves at harvest.

choices.label: Throw open the lord's barns
choices.text: {house}'s own barns are opened to {town} by the King's word.

ignore.text: {town} burns its bakeries and goes hungrier.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: {town} sends its children away
cards.text: Mothers in {town} put their children on carts to anywhere with bread. The roads fill with them.

choices.label: Take them in at Kingsmere
choices.text: The King's halls fill with {town}'s children.

later.text: {town}'s children grow up the King's own people.

choices.label: Send bread to {town} so they can stay
choices.text: Bread carts meet the children on the road.

choices.label: Close the roads
choices.text: The children turn back to {town}.

ignore.text: The children of {town} go where they can.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: {town} eats its horses
cards.text: The last horses in {town} are going into the pot. Without them there will be no ploughing.

choices.label: Send plough oxen for spring
choices.text: Oxen are driven to {town} under the crown's brand.

later.text: {town}'s fields are ploughed in time; the harvest comes.

choices.label: Send grain so the horses live
choices.text: Grain reaches {town}; the horses are spared.

choices.label: Let them eat
choices.text: {town} eats tonight, and starves next year.

later.text: {town}'s fields lie fallow without horses.

ignore.text: {town} eats its horses and its seed corn.

cards.subject: hungry_town
cards.title: Terrible rumours from {town}
cards.text: Travellers whisper about what the starving of {town} eat now. Nobody wants to say it at court.

choices.label: Send the royal granary's last
choices.text: The last of the crown's grain goes to {town}.

choices.label: Send priests and a physician
choices.text: The priests go to {town} and pray over what they find.

choices.label: Close {town} to travellers
choices.text: {town} is sealed until the hunger passes.

later.text: The tales from sealed {town} grow worse in every telling.

ignore.text: The whispers about {town} reach every hall.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A grain ship offers its cargo
cards.text: A southern captain has a hold full of wheat, and he knows what it is worth in a hungry realm.

choices.label: Pay his price
choices.text: The wheat comes ashore and goes inland.

choices.label: Seize the ship
choices.text: The captain is put ashore; the wheat is the crown's.

later.text: No southern ship will dock in the King's harbours.

choices.label: Haggle him down
choices.text: The captain sells for less, and sails off muttering.

later.text: The captain sold half his grain to a great house instead.

ignore.text: The ship sails on to a richer harbour.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Deserters on the roads
cards.text: Men are slipping away from the levies with their spears. Some go home; some go into the woods.

choices.label: Hang the deserters you catch
choices.text: Gibbets go up at the crossroads.

choices.label: Pay the levy on time
choices.text: The crown's pay chests ride out to every camp.

choices.label: Let the farmers go home
choices.text: The levy thins; the fields fill.

later.text: A thin levy meets the trouble.

ignore.text: The deserters become bandits.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A spy from the enemy camp
cards.text: A man was taken near the walls with a map of Kingsmere's gates sewn into his coat.

choices.label: Make him talk
choices.text: The spy talks; the King learns the enemy's numbers.

choices.label: Send him back with a false map
choices.text: The spy goes home with the wrong gates.

later.text: The enemy's men come to the wrong gate.

choices.label: Hang him from the gate
choices.text: The spy hangs where his friends can see him.

ignore.text: The spy slips his ropes in the night.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: Kingsmere's walls are old
cards.text: The master mason says the north wall is more ivy than stone. With trouble coming, someone should mend it.

choices.label: Mend it now, whatever the cost
choices.text: Masons swarm the north wall.

choices.label: Patch the worst of it
choices.text: Timber and earth fill the cracks.

choices.label: The walls have stood a hundred years
choices.text: The ivy stays.

later.text: The north wall slumps in the rain.

ignore.text: The north wall crumbles a little more.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The lords sit on their hands
cards.text: With trouble on the march, the great houses send letters full of excuses and no spears.

choices.label: Shame them in open court
choices.text: The King reads their letters aloud at Kingsmere.

choices.label: Buy their spears
choices.text: Silver goes out; spears come in.

choices.label: Fight without them
choices.text: The crown stands alone.

later.text: The lords who held back now say the King needed no help.

ignore.text: The lords wait to see who wins.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The old lords call the King a boy
cards.text: In the first seasons of a reign the grey lords test the crown. One of them yawned through the King's speech.

choices.label: Make an example of him
choices.text: The yawning lord loses his seat at court.

later.text: No lord yawns at court now.

choices.label: Win them over at table
choices.text: A season of feasts for the grey lords.

choices.label: Let deeds answer
choices.text: The King says nothing and gets to work.

ignore.text: The grey lords keep yawning.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The coronation is still unpaid
cards.text: The goldsmiths who made the crown want paying. So do the cooks, the heralds and the man who hired out the tents.

choices.label: Pay them all
choices.text: The crown's first debts are settled.

choices.label: Pay the goldsmiths only
choices.text: The cooks and heralds wait, and talk.

later.text: The unpaid heralds sing rude verses in the taverns.

choices.label: Tell them it was an honour to serve
choices.text: The tradesmen of Kingsmere remember it.

ignore.text: The goldsmiths' guild sues the crown before the temple.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The King's first hanging
cards.text: A horse thief waits on the scaffold at {town}. The crowd wants to see what kind of king they have.

choices.label: Pardon him
choices.text: The thief walks free; the crowd cheers a merciful king.

later.text: Every thief in {town} expects a pardon now.

choices.label: Let it be done
choices.text: The rope is used; the crowd goes home thinking.

choices.label: Send him to the levy instead
choices.text: The thief marches with the King's spears.

ignore.text: The thief is hanged without the King, and the crowd notes it.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The treasury is nearly bare
cards.text: The steward turns the last chest on its side. The guards' pay is due next season.

choices.label: Melt the royal plate
choices.text: The King eats off pewter; the guards are paid.

choices.label: Borrow from the moneylenders
choices.text: The moneylenders open their chests, and their ledgers.

later.text: The moneylenders come for their silver, and more.

choices.label: A special levy on every house
choices.text: Every great house pays toward the crown.

ignore.text: The guards go unpaid, and grumble at the gates.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The steward has never seen so much silver
cards.text: The treasury's chests are full. The lords notice, and so do the beggars.

choices.label: Build something to be remembered by
choices.text: A royal work is begun at Kingsmere.

later.text: The King's great work stands; travellers come to see it.

choices.label: Give a gift to every house
choices.text: Every great house gets a chest from the King.

choices.label: Keep it; lean years come
choices.text: The chests stay full, and closely watched.

ignore.text: The lords whisper that the King is a miser.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The steward's new house
cards.text: The steward has built a fine house in {town}. The steward's pay would not build a henhouse.

choices.label: Audit the books
choices.text: The King's clerks open the steward's ledgers.

later.text: The steward's thefts are found and repaid.

choices.label: Dismiss him quietly
choices.text: A new steward takes the keys.

choices.label: A good steward deserves a good house
choices.text: The steward keeps the house, and the habit.

later.text: The steward's thefts grow bolder.

ignore.text: The steward builds a stable next.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The Hand and the Marshal at each other's throats
cards.text: Every council the Hand and the Marshal shout over each other. The clerks have stopped writing it down.

choices.label: Side with the Hand
choices.text: The Marshal sulks among his soldiers.

later.text: The Marshal's men are slow to answer the Hand's orders.

choices.label: Side with the Marshal
choices.text: The Hand counts coins louder than before.

later.text: The Hand's purse is slow to pay the Marshal's men.

choices.label: Make them dine together
choices.text: A long, silent supper. Then a slightly less silent one.

ignore.text: The council stops deciding anything.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: A painter wants to paint the King
cards.text: A famous painter from abroad offers a portrait of the King, for a price, and a season of sittings.

choices.label: Sit for the portrait
choices.text: The portrait hangs in {town}'s great hall.

later.text: The King's portrait is copied for every great house.

choices.label: Have him paint the court instead
choices.text: The painter sketches the lords; the lords love it.

choices.label: The King has no time for sittings
choices.text: The painter goes to a rival court.

ignore.text: The painter paints a great lord instead, in the King's pose.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The astrologer's warning
cards.text: The court astrologer says the stars warn against travel this year. The King has three journeys planned.

choices.label: Stay home
choices.text: The journeys are cancelled; the lords who expected the King wait.

choices.label: Travel anyway
choices.text: The King rides out; the astrologer wrings his hands.

later.text: The King returned safe; the astrologer looks for a new post.

choices.label: Find a better astrologer
choices.text: A new astrologer reads kinder stars.

ignore.text: The astrologer tells everyone what the stars said.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A foreign envoy will not kneel
cards.text: An envoy from over the sea stands upright before the throne. The court holds its breath.

choices.label: Make him kneel
choices.text: The guards bend his knee for him.

later.text: Over the sea they call the King a tyrant, and tax his ships.

choices.label: Laugh and wave him on
choices.text: The envoy speaks standing; some lords think the King weak.

choices.label: Rise and greet him as an equal
choices.text: The King steps down to the envoy; the court gasps.

later.text: The envoy's country sends ships of trade.

ignore.text: The envoy leaves, unseen and unpleased.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The King's cousin marries
cards.text: The King's cousin weds a minor lady. A royal wedding means a royal feast, or a royal slight.

choices.label: A feast fit for a prince
choices.text: Every house sends someone; everyone eats.

choices.label: A family supper
choices.text: The cousin is wed quietly, and resents it.

later.text: The cousin leaves court for the cold houses' company.

choices.label: Let the bride's family pay
choices.text: The bride's family feast the realm, and own the day.

ignore.text: The cousin weds without the King's blessing.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Knights errant at court
cards.text: A band of landless knights asks to serve the King. They have more swords than manners.

choices.label: Take them into the guard
choices.text: The knights eat the King's bread and wear his colours.

choices.label: Send them against the outlaws
choices.text: The knights ride off to hunt for glory and bandits.

later.text: The knights errant clear the King's roads of thieves.

choices.label: No more mouths at court
choices.text: The knights ride on to a lord who will feed them.

later.text: The knights errant fight for a great house now.

ignore.text: The knights brawl in Kingsmere's taverns.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The lords grow fat in peace
cards.text: Years without war, and the lords are bored. Boredom makes plotters.

choices.label: Hold a great tourney
choices.text: The lords break lances instead of oaths.

choices.label: Send them on a crusade abroad
choices.text: The restless young lords sail away to a far war.

later.text: The young lords come home scarred, and humbler.

choices.label: Let them plot; it keeps them busy
choices.text: The plotting starts.

later.text: A plot against the crown is whispered of.

ignore.text: Boredom finds its own amusement.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Who comes after the King?
cards.text: The King's hair is greying. The lords ask, less quietly each year, who will wear the crown next.

choices.label: Name an heir before the court
choices.text: The heir is proclaimed at Kingsmere.

later.text: The lords court the heir now, as much as the King.

choices.label: Say the gods will choose
choices.text: The question hangs over every feast.

choices.label: Make the lords swear to whoever you name later
choices.text: The lords swear to a name not yet spoken.

ignore.text: Each great house backs its own heir in whispers.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The chronicler wants the King's own words
cards.text: The court chronicler is writing the history of the reign and wants to hear it from the King's mouth.

choices.label: Tell it all, the bad with the good
choices.text: The chronicle is honest; the lords read it with surprise.

choices.label: Tell only the triumphs
choices.text: The chronicle shines; nobody believes all of it.

later.text: Later readers call the chronicle flattery.

choices.label: Pay him to write it himself
choices.text: The chronicler writes what he thinks the King wants.

ignore.text: The chronicler writes it from tavern talk.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: An old enemy's son comes to court
cards.text: The son of a lord the King once broke asks to serve. He smiles a great deal.

choices.label: Take him into service
choices.text: He serves, and smiles.

later.text: The son serves faithfully; the old feud is buried.

choices.label: Watch him closely
choices.text: A spy sleeps outside the son's door.

choices.label: Send him away
choices.text: The son leaves, still smiling.

later.text: The son is seen at a cold house's table.

ignore.text: The son finds another lord to serve.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: A southern prince offers an alliance
cards.text: A prince from beyond the hills sends an envoy: spears for the King's wars, ports for his ships.

choices.label: Sign the alliance
choices.text: The King's seal goes on the treaty.

later.text: The southern prince calls on the alliance; the crown must send men.

choices.label: Trade only, no spears
choices.text: A trading treaty is signed.

later.text: Southern ships fill the King's ports with goods.

choices.label: No foreign ties
choices.text: The envoy goes home.

ignore.text: The southern prince signs with a great house instead.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: The King's physician quarrels with the priests
cards.text: The physician wants to cut and study the dead; the priests say it is a sin.

choices.label: Side with the physician
choices.text: The physician studies; the priests preach against it.

later.text: The physician's learning saves a lord's heir at {town}.

choices.label: Side with the priests
choices.text: The physician burns his notes.

choices.label: Let him study in secret
choices.text: The physician works by night, behind locked doors.

ignore.text: The priests drive the physician out of {town}.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: A song about the King in {town}'s taverns
cards.text: Every tavern in {town} is singing a new song about the King. It is not kind.

choices.label: Find the singer and reward a better song
choices.text: The singer writes a kinder verse, for a purse.

choices.label: Ban the song
choices.text: The song is banned, so everyone sings it louder.

later.text: The banned song is sung in every town now.

choices.label: Sing it yourself at supper
choices.text: The King sings the song at his own table; the court roars.

later.text: The taverns of {town} sing the King's own verse now, and laugh with him.

ignore.text: The song spreads to the next town.

cards.subject: seat
cards.title: A stone is missing from the crown
cards.text: The great red stone in the crown has been prised out and replaced with glass. Nobody knows when.

choices.label: Turn the castle upside down
choices.text: Every room at {town} is searched.

later.text: The stone is found sewn into a page's jacket.

choices.label: Wear the glass and say nothing
choices.text: The King wears glass; nobody notices.

later.text: A jeweller in a great house sells a famous red stone.

choices.label: Offer a reward for its return
choices.text: A reward is cried in every market.

later.text: The stone comes back, wrapped in a beggar's rag.

ignore.text: The theft becomes a joke at court.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The old chancellor wants to retire
cards.text: The chancellor who served three kings asks leave to go home. Nobody else knows where the papers are.

choices.label: Give him a pension and a manor
choices.text: The old chancellor retires in honour.

choices.label: Ask him to stay one more year
choices.text: The chancellor sighs, and stays.

later.text: The old chancellor dies at his desk, papers in order.

choices.label: Let him go
choices.text: The chancellor goes; the papers are a mess for a season.

ignore.text: The chancellor leaves without a farewell.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The lords say the crown hoards grain
cards.text: Word is going round that Kingsmere's granaries are full while the realm goes hungry.

choices.label: Open the granaries to the lords
choices.text: The lords' carts fill at Kingsmere.

choices.label: Show the empty granaries
choices.text: The lords are walked through bare barns.

choices.label: Let them talk
choices.text: The rumour grows with the hunger.

later.text: The lords repeat the rumour as fact.

ignore.text: The rumour becomes the truth people tell.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Wolves on the winter roads
cards.text: Couriers come in with torn cloaks. The packs are bold this year.

choices.label: Escort every courier
choices.text: Couriers ride with spears this winter.

choices.label: Pay a bounty on wolves
choices.text: Wolf pelts pile up at every town gate.

later.text: The roads are quieter; the bounty did it.

choices.label: The couriers ride fast enough
choices.text: A courier goes missing.

later.text: A courier's horse comes back without him.

ignore.text: The King's letters arrive late, if at all.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: Spring floods at {town}
cards.text: The meltwater burst the dykes at {town}. Fields are lakes; cottages are islands.

choices.label: Rebuild the dykes in stone
choices.text: Stone dykes rise around {town}'s fields.

later.text: The next flood breaks on {town}'s new dykes and goes no further.

choices.label: Send boats and bread
choices.text: Boats ferry {town}'s folk to dry ground.

choices.label: The water will go down
choices.text: The water goes down, slowly.

ignore.text: {town}'s spring sowing is lost.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: {house} disputes the harvest tithe
cards.text: {lord} says the crown's reeves counted the sheaves twice. {house}'s barns at {town} say otherwise.

choices.label: Recount the sheaves
choices.text: The reeves count again at {town}.

later.text: The recount finds {house} was right.

choices.label: The tithe stands
choices.text: {house} pays, and protests.

choices.label: Halve it for {house}
choices.text: {house} pays half; other houses ask why.

ignore.text: {house} pays nothing this autumn.

cards.subject: house_any
cards.title: A wedding ends in blood at {town}
cards.text: At a wedding in {house}'s hall, an old feud came out with the wine. Two guests are dead.

choices.label: Send the King's justice
choices.text: A royal judge rides to {town}.

later.text: The killers hang; {house} says the King's justice is fair.

choices.label: Leave it to {lord}
choices.text: {lord} judges in their own hall.

choices.label: Fine every family there
choices.text: Every family at the wedding pays the crown.

ignore.text: The feud spreads through {house}'s lands.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {house} founds a monastery
cards.text: {lord} would found a monastery near {town} and name the King its patron.

choices.label: Be its patron
choices.text: The King's name is carved over the gate at {town}.

choices.label: Let {house} have the honour
choices.text: {house}'s name alone goes over the gate.

choices.label: Land for monks is land lost to tithe
choices.text: {lord} builds it smaller.

ignore.text: {house} builds it, and names a saint instead of the King.

cards.subject: house_cold
cards.title: {house} shelters a heretic preacher
cards.text: A preacher who calls the King's priests liars is living at {town} as {lord}'s guest.

choices.label: Demand they hand him over
choices.text: {lord} is ordered to hand the preacher to the King's priests.

choices.label: Let him preach
choices.text: The preacher preaches; the priests are furious.

later.text: The preacher's followers grow in {town}.

choices.label: Invite him to debate at court
choices.text: The preacher comes to Kingsmere to argue with the high priest.

later.text: The debate is the talk of the realm; both sides claim victory.

ignore.text: The preacher's words spread from {town}.

cards.subject: house_warm
cards.title: {lord} offers a champion
cards.text: {house} has a giant of a knight, and {lord} would see him fight under the King's banner.

choices.label: Make him the King's champion
choices.text: The giant stands at the King's right hand.

choices.label: Let him fight in the lists
choices.text: The giant unhorses every knight in the realm.

choices.label: The King has knights enough
choices.text: The giant goes home to {town}.

ignore.text: The giant fights for a rival court.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Foreign merchants want a fair
cards.text: Merchants from over the sea would hold a great fair in the realm, if the King guarantees their safety.

choices.label: Guarantee it with the King's guard
choices.text: The fair is held under the crown's banner.

later.text: The foreign fair comes every year now, and pays well.

choices.label: Guarantee it with words
choices.text: The fair comes; a merchant is robbed.

later.text: The robbed merchant tells every port of it.

choices.label: Our own merchants come first
choices.text: The guilds cheer; the foreigners stay home.

ignore.text: The fair goes to a great house's town instead.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: {town}'s weavers want a monopoly
cards.text: The weavers of {town} want no cloth sold there but theirs. They offer the crown a fee for it.

choices.label: Sell them the monopoly
choices.text: {town}'s weavers pay, and raise their prices.

choices.label: Refuse; trade stays free
choices.text: The weavers sulk at their looms.

later.text: Cheap cloth floods {town}; the weavers grumble, the people don't.

choices.label: Grant it for ten years only
choices.text: The weavers pay a little, and plan to ask again.

ignore.text: The weavers break the looms of anyone who competes.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: The mine at {town} floods
cards.text: Water broke into the deep shafts at {town}. The miners got out; the silver did not.

choices.label: Build pumps
choices.text: Great wheels and pumps are raised at {town}.

later.text: The pumps clear the shafts; silver flows again.

choices.label: Dig a new shaft higher up
choices.text: A new shaft is begun.

later.text: The new shaft finds a thin vein.

choices.label: Close the mine
choices.text: The miners of {town} look for other work.

ignore.text: {town}'s miners drift away.

cards.subject: crown_town
cards.title: A toll bridge at {town}?
cards.text: {town}'s new bridge brings travellers. The steward says a penny a crossing would pay for it twice over.

choices.label: Toll it
choices.text: Every traveller pays at {town}'s bridge.

later.text: Merchants find a ford upstream.

choices.label: Keep it free
choices.text: The bridge stays free; {town}'s market grows.

later.text: {town}'s market doubles; the crown's share grows with it.

choices.label: Toll only foreigners
choices.text: Foreign merchants pay; locals cross free.

ignore.text: {town} tolls the bridge itself, and keeps it.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: Settlers want the empty lands
cards.text: Landless families ask leave to clear the wild country beyond the last royal town.

choices.label: Grant them land and tools
choices.text: The families go out with axes and the King's blessing.

later.text: A new village thrives in the wild country, loyal to the crown.

choices.label: Grant land, no tools
choices.text: The families go with only their hands.

later.text: Half the settlers come back hungry.

choices.label: The wild country is the King's hunting ground
choices.text: The families stay landless.

ignore.text: The families go anyway, and owe the crown nothing.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The sweating sickness
cards.text: A sickness that kills in a day is going through the towns. The lords are leaving for their country seats.

choices.label: Close the court
choices.text: The court scatters; the King waits it out.

later.text: The sickness passes; the court returns, fewer.

choices.label: Stay at Kingsmere and be seen
choices.text: The King stays; the realm notices.

later.text: A dozen at court sicken; the King is spared.

choices.label: Pay physicians in every town
choices.text: Physicians go out on the crown's silver.

ignore.text: The sickness runs its course through the realm.

cards.subject: realm
cards.title: The lords want a jubilee
cards.text: The reign has been long. The great houses would celebrate it, and see what the King gives them.

choices.label: A jubilee for the realm
choices.text: Bonfires burn on every hill for the King's long reign.

choices.label: A feast at Kingsmere
choices.text: The lords feast; the towns don't.

choices.label: A reign is not a festival
choices.text: The lords go home disappointed.

ignore.text: The lords celebrate without the King.
